reference: Hoebeke, Y., Blanchard, M. A., Contreras, A., & Heeren, A. (2022). An experience sampling measure of the key features of rumination. Clinical Neuropsychiatry, 19(5), 288-297.

date.tz_evidence: The deposit's formr survey (FE_RUM_survey v2_EN.csv, osf.io/dngyk) sets timezone "CET" and prompts at 09:00, 13:00, 17:00 and 21:00; the stamps as written cluster at exactly 9, 13, 17 and 21h, and do not shift at the 2021-03-28 DST change, as true UTC stamps would. So the Z stamps are Belgian local time.

tables.name: hoebeke_2022_rumination
tables.description: Experience sampling, 4 prompts a day (9am, 1pm, 5pm, 9pm) for 14 days, community sample of 40 French-speaking adults: five items on key features of rumination since the previous prompt (perseverance, negativity, self-criticism, brooding, replaying). 0-100 sliders.

items.stem: How much time did you spend thinking of one or more emotional experiences?
To what extent were your thoughts negative?
"To what extent were your thoughts self -critical?"
How much did you think about the causes and consequences of emotional experiences?
To what extent have you mentally replayed emotional experiences that you’ve had?

not_shipped.activity: single item (absorption in activity) for a larger project; not part of the measure (paper, footnote 2)
not_shipped.att_control: single item (executive control) for a larger project; not part of the measure (paper, footnote 2)

itemtext.why: No item text for this PR, per #3421.

notes: formr would not submit a prompt until every slider had been moved off its default of 50 (the submit item's showif in FE_RUM_survey v2_EN.csv), so no response is exactly 50.

The OSF raw file (ESM-RUM_02_ESM.csv) has three more answered rows than openESM's copy; each is a second submission started the moment the previous answer to the same prompt ended. openESM keeps the first. Every shipped value matches the raw file.

The paper (footnote 4) removed one observation submitted 289 minutes after its prompt. openESM's copy already excludes it, as does the OSF raw file: the longest gap between prompt and submission in either is 153 minutes.

For whoever does item text: participants answered in French. The authors developed the items in French and back-translated them into English (paper; Table S1 of the supplement, osf.io/wj6xn), and openESM's English wording is that back-translation.
For the openESM report (#1698): 0013_hoebeke's created/modified/ended/expired stamps carry a Z but hold Belgian local time.

flags.what: `wave` = each person's prompts numbered in created order (openESM time columns, best first: ['created', 'ended', 'modified', 'expired']). `date` = created as Unix seconds. Data run 2021-02-26 09:01 .. 2021-06-08 21:23 as written. Set date.window from the paper's collection period.
flags.resolution: wave = each person's prompts numbered in time order of created; date = created in Unix seconds. openESM's counter agrees with that order. date.window is the paper's collection period, 'between February 26th, 2021 and June 8th, 2021', with the end set to 2021-06-09 so that June 8 is included.

flags.what: Time zone of created. Written with a `Z`, but in 0072_neubauer and 0056/0057_ryvkina the `Z` stamps are local time. Hour-of-day counts as written: 9h:342, 10h:157, 11h:1, 13h:456, 14h:77, 15h:1, 17h:433, 18h:87, 19h:9, 21h:447, 22h:92. No Unix time column to check against: compare with the paper. Set date.tz to 'UTC' if the stamps are true UTC, or to the study's IANA zone (e.g. 'Europe/Berlin') if they are local time, and say how you know in date.tz_evidence.
flags.resolution: Europe/Brussels, not UTC: see date.tz_evidence (formr timezone CET, prompts at 9/13/17/21h, no shift at the DST change).

flags.what: Tables are a first guess from file order, response scale, source, prompts asked at, and column-name prefixes. Read the codebook and split or merge so each table is one instrument or subscale (datastandard.md, 'One file per scale'); rename each `<author>_<year>_<construct>`, and set `script` to the record's name.
flags.resolution: One table, hoebeke_2022_rumination: the five 0-100 slider items the paper develops and validates as its measure.

flags.what: `candidates` holds columns that may or may not be items (binary checkboxes, counts, rating scales whose coding gives no anchors -- activity, att_control). Move any that are responses into a table; the rest go to `not_shipped` with a reason. activity, att_control
flags.resolution: activity and att_control go to not_shipped: the paper (footnote 2) describes them as 'two additional items assessing self-report executive control and self-report absorption in an activity' for a larger project; single items, not part of the measure, and not in the deposit's ESM survey file.

flags.what: openESM says cross-sectional (baseline) data exist. Covariates such as age and gender are not handled by this tool: add them by hand to the generated script if wanted (neubauer_2023_stecco does), or note why not.
flags.resolution: No covariates. Age and gender are in the deposit's demographics file if wanted later.

flags.resolution: 'some variable codings unclear' concerns activity and att_control, settled by the paper's footnote 2.
